summary: Use a Skeleton group to show the shape of content while it loads, so the screen doesn't jump when it arrives.

useWhen.text: Show the shape of content while it loads, with a SkeletonGroup, so the screen doesn't jump when it arrives.

from.quote: Use a Skeleton group to show the shape of content while it loads, so the screen doesn't jump when it arrives.

useWhen.text: Show the shape of what's coming, then fill it in place.

useWhen.text: Refreshing a list, such as holdings: the rows go into their loading state, then the content swaps back in place.

configuration.text: Inside a group, Coin components such as Text, Avatar, Badge, and Button draw their own placeholder at their own size, so you rarely place a Skeleton by hand.

configuration.text: A SkeletonGroup switches every placeholder inside it; Text, Avatar, Badge, Button, Image and other Coin components draw their own, and a Skeleton places one by hand.

examples.purpose: Refreshing holdings, the guide's In context: the screen sets the group's loading while it refreshes the holdings, then turns it off and the content swaps back in place. The title and the button sit outside the group and stay real; each Text and Badge in the rows draws its own placeholder.
examples.jsx:
<VStack>
  <Text>Your holdings</Text>
  <SkeletonGroup loading>
    <HStack alignVertical="center">
      <VStack style={{ flex: 1 }}>
        <Text>Reliance Industries</Text>
        <Text>64 units · ₹1,52,900</Text>
      </VStack>
      <Badge label="Equity" />
    </HStack>
    <HStack alignVertical="center">
      <VStack style={{ flex: 1 }}>
        <Text>HDFC Bank</Text>
        <Text>120 units · ₹1,98,400</Text>
      </VStack>
      <Badge label="Equity" />
    </HStack>
  </SkeletonGroup>
  <Button label="Refresh" onPress={() => {}} />
</VStack>

from.quote: Refresh puts the holdings into their loading state for two seconds, then swaps the content back in place. The title and the button stay real.

examples.purpose: Known title, loading values: the heading is inside the loading group but keeps loading={false}, so it stays readable; only the values still loading turn into placeholders.

</SkeletonGroup>

examples.purpose: Placeholders placed by hand, the guide's anatomy: one Skeleton of each kind inside a loading group, each given its own width and height. kind sets only the corners.
examples.jsx:
<SkeletonGroup loading>
  <VStack>
    <Skeleton kind="text" width={220} height={20} />
    <Skeleton kind="image" width={220} height={120} />
    <Skeleton kind="badge" width={70} height={20} />
    <Skeleton kind="other" width={48} height={48} />
  </VStack>
</SkeletonGroup>

from.quote: Each placeholder is a light grey block whose kind sets its corners.

props.name: kind
props.description: kind sets only the corner radius: text and other 9999 (a full pill, or a circle when square), image 10, badge 4. Declared: Visual category — controls only the corner-radius token. Sizes are still supplied via `width`/`height`. Defaults to `'other'`. Default "other", from the component source.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the rectangular placeholder. Numbers are dp, strings are RN dimensions.

props.name: style
props.description: Optional style overrides merged onto the base layer (e.g. `marginTop`, `alignSelf`). Avoid `backgroundColor` and `borderRadius` here — use the design tokens instead so the system stays consistent.

props.name: modes
props.description: Modes for token resolution (forwarded to `getVariableByName`). Most consumers can omit this — defaults work for every standard mode.

props.name: visible
props.description: A visible placeholder draws with no group, runs its own shimmer, and is a progressbar named “Loading”. Primitives set it from their own loading. Declared: Draw the placeholder even when no `SkeletonGroup` is loading. Primitives set this when their own `loading` prop is true. A sprinkled `<Skeleton />` leaves it unset, so an idle group still hides it. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: SkeletonGroup.loading
props.description: On SkeletonGroup, required: while true, every Skeleton and every Coin component that draws its own placeholder inside the group shows its placeholder, except a component that sets loading={false}; a nested group replaces the outer one. false shows the content.

props.name: SkeletonGroup.reducedMotion
props.description: On SkeletonGroup: left unset, the group follows the device's reduced-motion setting; true or false forces it.

modes.name: context5
modes.description: Not in the package's mode list for Skeleton, but it sets the block colour: Default is light grey (#e7e7e7) in every Color Mode; Fullscreen Modal is deep brown (rgb(44, 37, 27)) in Light. FullscreenModal always passes it to its content.
